name: Jes Staley

summary.text: James 'Jes' Staley is a former chief executive of Barclays. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority banned him from senior management roles in financial services and fined him over a letter to the regulator, approved by Staley, that contained misleading statements about his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. On June 26, 2025 the Upper Tribunal upheld the ban, finding a lack of integrity and failures to be open with the FCA, and reduced the fine from £1.8 million to £1.1 million; the FCA issued its Final Notice on July 23, 2025.

sources.title: Upper Tribunal upholds Jes Staley ban

facts.claim: The Upper Tribunal upheld the FCA's decision to ban Staley, former chief executive of Barclays, from holding senior management roles in the financial services industry; the FCA issued a Final Notice on July 23, 2025 following the Tribunal's June 26, 2025 decision.
facts.quote: The FCA's decision to ban Jes Staley, former CEO of Barclays, from holding senior management roles in the financial services industry has been upheld by the Upper Tribunal.

sources.title: Upper Tribunal upholds Jes Staley ban

facts.claim: The FCA's case concerned a letter to the regulator approved by Staley that contained misleading statements about the nature of his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and their last point of contact; the letter said he was not close to Epstein, while in emails Staley had described Epstein as one of his 'deepest' and 'most cherished' friends.
facts.quote: Mr Staley approved a letter sent to the FCA that contained misleading statements about the nature of his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and their last point of contact.

sources.title: Upper Tribunal upholds Jes Staley ban

facts.claim: The Tribunal found a lack of integrity, a failure to be open and co-operative with the FCA, and a failure to make appropriate disclosures.

sources.title: Upper Tribunal upholds Jes Staley ban

facts.claim: The FCA had proposed a fine of £1.8 million; the Tribunal reduced it to £1.1 million because, after the FCA's Decision Notice, Barclays decided not to permit Staley to receive deferred shares to which he could have been entitled.
facts.quote: The Tribunal reduced this fine to £1.1m as, after the FCA issued its Decision Notice, Barclays decided not to permit Mr Staley to receive deferred shares to which he could have been entitled.
